stories.headline: EU calls for border action after mass migrant crossings in Ceuta
stories.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has called for united action on border security following mass migrant crossings into Ceuta. Ceuta and Melilla represent the European Union's only land borders with Africa.

Spain estimates that approximately 69,500 migrants have returned to Morocco after entering Ceuta. However, Ceuta's top government official Juan Jesus Vivas estimated that between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants remained in the city after initial returns. Following the crossings, Spanish officials began installing a 500-metre floating barrier at the border with Morocco.

Casualties have been reported on both sides of the border. The official death toll stands at 72 on the Spanish side and 11 on the Moroccan side. Meanwhile, the Moroccan Association for Human Rights reported nearly 130 victims and dozens missing from the border rush.

The crisis has caused political reactions across Europe. Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen border-free arrangement with Spain following the crossings. Additionally, Italy and Denmark organised a letter signed by 22 EU member states criticizing Spain's regularisation of undocumented migrants.

stories.headline: Donald Trump insists US-Iran negotiations are underway as Tehran denies direct talks
stories.body:
United States President Donald Trump has stated that negotiations with Iran are ongoing, calling them a last chance before decapitation. In contrast, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei explicitly denied direct talks with Washington. Baqaei stated that negotiations are instead being held with Oman over vessel passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

The conflict comes during an active war between the United States and Iran, which began on February 28, 2026, following surprise strikes by the United States and Israel. Following Tehran's public denial of direct discussions, Donald Trump called the Iranian leadership unbelievably duplicitous on Truth Social for denying negotiations.

At the same time, Donald Trump stated that he called off planned military strikes on Iran. According to Trump, he made this decision at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar.

The announcements surrounding potential US-Iran negotiations have already influenced energy markets and maritime trade. Brent Crude oil fell by 4.5% to $83.98 per barrel following announcements regarding potential negotiations. Meanwhile, shipping through the region has dropped sharply. Vessel crossings in the Strait of Hormuz dropped to 51 between July 30 and August 2, according to data from Kpler.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian beach kills seven as Moscow restaurant is bombed
stories.body:
Seven people, including three children, were killed when drone debris struck a beach in Arkhipo-Osipovka. Krasnodar region Governor Veniamin Kondratyev stated that 40 people were injured and 17 hospitalised in the Arkhipo-Osipovka beach strike. Reports also noted that a drone struck a crowded beach near the Russian Black Sea resort of Gelendzhik.

Following the beach strike, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused NATO and the European Union of participating in international terrorist activity. Overnight, another Ukrainian drone strike targeted a Wildberries warehouse in the Vladimir region.

In a separate violence incident in Russia, a bombing at an Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow killed five people and injured 19 others. Reports indicated that the Moscow restaurant bombing may have targeted Colonel General Alexander Chaiko during his 55th birthday celebration.

stories.headline: Europe heatwave and low river levels strain energy output and force evacuations
stories.body:
Severe weather conditions are creating energy and safety challenges across Europe. England and Wales recorded their driest July in nearly 200 years of recordkeeping, according to the Met Office. Water levels on the River Rhine dropped to historic record lows at Cologne in Germany and Lobith in the Netherlands.

Low water levels on the Danube River have severely affected power generation. Hungary reduced output at the Paks nuclear power plant to little more than 10% capacity due to low Danube water levels. In response, the Romanian military detonated a rocky outcrop in the Danube to direct cooling water flow to the Cernavoda nuclear power plant. Romanian naval forces used 180 kg of explosives in a controlled underwater explosion to restore water flow near Cernavoda. Due to the national energy crisis, carmakers Dacia and Ford agreed to suspend automotive production in Romania until August 19.

Wildfires and firefighting operations have also turned deadly. In France, authorities evacuated over 224,000 people due to a massive wildfire burning 420 square kilometres in the country's largest civilian evacuation outside wartime. West of Athens, two crew members died in a midair helicopter collision during firefighting operations.

stories.headline: Ousted Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross in first external contact in two years
stories.body:
Ousted Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi has met an International Committee of the Red Cross delegation led by Arnaud de Baecque in Naypyitaw. The meeting represents her first external contact in two years. Her son, Kim Aris, described his mother's meeting with the Red Cross representative as the first positive development concerning her in over five years.

Aung San Suu Kyi was detained in 2021 after a military coup and sentenced to 33 years in prison before being moved to house arrest. Official photos released by Myanmar authorities showed Aung San Suu Kyi cutting an 81st birthday cake.

Myanmar authorities continue to enforce strict rules regarding the former leader. A Yangon court sentenced former lawmaker Saw Naing to three years in prison for organizing a religious ceremony on Aung San Suu Kyi's birthday.

stories.headline: US and Japan perform joint currency intervention to support the yen
stories.body:
Japan and the United States have executed a joint currency intervention to strengthen the Japanese yen. Following the intervention, the Japanese yen strengthened to 155 to the US dollar. Prior to the market intervention, the Japanese yen had fallen to a 40-year low of nearly 164 to the US dollar.

Bank of Japan data indicated that Tokyo spent as much as $36.58 billion on Friday to support the yen. In Washington, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted on his cabinet meeting pad a task to buy $5 billion to $10 billion worth of Japanese yen.

This market intervention was the first joint foreign exchange action conducted by the United States and Japan since March 2011. At the time of the action, the Bank of Japan maintained its main interest rate at 1% while the US Federal Reserve's benchmark rate stood between 3.50% and 3.75%.

stories.headline: Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin flees to France amid political pressure
stories.body:
Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin has fled Russia to Paris as government pressure against him intensified. Nadezhdin posted a video from Paris confirming he had left Russia after being prevented from running for parliament.

The Russian government had placed repeated political and legal restrictions on Nadezhdin. Russia's justice ministry designated Boris Nadezhdin as a foreign agent and barred him from parliamentary elections. Previously, Russian electoral authorities barred Boris Nadezhdin from running in the 2024 presidential election citing flawed candidate signatures.

In addition to electoral bans, Nadezhdin faced legal charges. Boris Nadezhdin was charged with displaying extremist symbols over a 10-second image of Alexei Navalny in a reposted social media video.

stories.headline: Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj wins Bihar byelection in Bankipur
stories.body:
Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor has won the Bankipur Assembly byelection in Bihar, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes. The victory ends a long political tenure, as the BJP had held the Bankipur Assembly seat in Bihar for over three decades since 1995 prior to Prashant Kishor's victory. The Bankipur seat became vacant after BJP leader Nitin Nabin resigned upon his election to the Rajya Sabha and elevation to BJP national president.

In the Bankipur race, independent candidates named Lalu Prasad Yadav and Nitish Kumar received 81 and 149 votes respectively, losing their security deposits.

Results were also announced for assembly byelections in other Indian states. In Gujarat, BJP candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel won the Manjalpur Assembly seat by a margin of 30,630 votes. Meanwhile, in Madhya Pradesh, Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh won the Datia Assembly byelection by 6,016 votes.

stories.headline: Delhi court acquits former wrestling chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in harassment case
stories.body:
A New Delhi court has acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in a sexual harassment case filed by six female wrestlers. In the same ruling, former Wrestling Federation of India assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was acquitted of criminal intimidation charges by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar.

The verdict follows years of legal proceedings and public protests. Delhi Police registered two FIRs against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in April 2023 following complaints by female wrestlers. Prominent wrestlers including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia launched a sit-in protest against Singh at Jantar Mantar in April 2023. In May 2025, a Delhi court accepted a police closure report in a POCSO case against Singh after a minor complainant withdrew her allegations.

Following the court's verdict, wrestler Vinesh Phogat stated that the complainants will appeal Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's acquittal in a higher court.
